answer: Bonded vouching makes sybils costly: a new agent gains influence only when established peers stake collateral to vouch for it. A fake identity, light as a zephyr, cannot drift in unbacked; it must coax real agents to lock deposits. If the newcomer later defrauds, vouchers are slashed, so colluders burn capital on every fraud. One operator spinning up an island of a thousand clones leaves a traceable plume of self-vouching stake, which the honest graph refuses, pricing each fake far above its payoff.
